/-!
# Erdős Problem 152

#TODO: Formalize the corresponding conjecture for infinite Sidon sets.

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/152](https://www.erdosproblems.com/152)
 - [DM26a] DeepMind prover agent, [formal proof of Erdős problem 152](https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/29c60aa79729701905cf9e92517af23f588971f2/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L485) (2026)
 - [DM26b] DeepMind prover agent, [formal proof of the quadratic variant of Erdős problem 152](https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/ff58c933d53bb807bf85d98a47402703f9f14ed3/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L496) (2026)
 - [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number
    Theory (1994), 329-347.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise Asymptotics
open Filter

namespace Erdos152

/-- Define `f n` to be the minimum of `|{s | s - 1 ∉ A + A, s ∈ A + A, s + 1 ∉ A + A}|` as `A`
ranges over all Sidon sets of size `n`. -/
noncomputable def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ⨅ A : {A : Set ℕ | A.ncard = n ∧ IsSidon A},
  {s : ℕ | s - 1 ∉ A.1 + A.1 ∧ s ∈ A.1 + A.1 ∧ s + 1 ∉ A.1 + A.1}.ncard

/--
Must `lim f n = ∞`?

This was proved formally by the DeepMind prover agent [DM26a].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/29c60aa79729701905cf9e92517af23f588971f2/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L485"]
theorem erdos_152 : answer(True) ↔ Tendsto f atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Must `f n ≫ n ^ 2`?

This stronger quadratic variant was also proved formally by the DeepMind prover agent [DM26b].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/ff58c933d53bb807bf85d98a47402703f9f14ed3/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L496"]
theorem erdos_152.variants.square : answer(True) ↔
    (fun n => f n : ℕ → ℝ) ≫ (fun n => n ^ 2 : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos152

reformulations.difference: The helper counts isolated sums using truncated natural-number subtraction `s - 1`. So `s = 0` is never counted, even when 0 is isolated in the source's sense (0 ∈ A and 1 ∉ A, so -1 and 1 are both missing from A+A). It also ranges over `A : Set ℕ` that may contain 0, whereas erdosproblems.com uses the positive integers. Finally, `f 0` takes junk values from infinite sets with `ncard = 0` (irrelevant here). As a result `f n` can be one less than the source's minimum: Lean proves `f 1 = 0` via `A = {0}`, where the source's value is 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every A : Set ℕ, let S be the Lean isolated set and T the isolated set computed in ℤ. Then cast '' S ⊆ T ⊆ cast '' S ∪ {0}, so cntN A ≤ cntZ A ≤ cntN A + 1; this holds with no finiteness assumption, because both sets are infinite together. Translation A ↦ A+1 preserves the Sidon property, the size and the ℤ-count, and removes 0. Hence f n ≤ g n ≤ f n + 1, where g n is the source's minimum over Sidon sets of positive integers of size n (ℤ-count). Both theorems in the file are asymptotic (`Tendsto … atTop atTop`, `=O[atTop]`), and both are invariant under a perturbation bounded by 1. Proved sorry-free in /workspace/review/equiv.lean: `tendsto_iff : Tendsto f atTop atTop ↔ Tendsto g atTop atTop` and `isBigO_iff : (n² =O[atTop] f) ↔ (n² =O[atTop] g)`.

reformulations.difference: The source states "For any M ≥ 1, if A ⊂ ℕ is a sufficiently large finite Sidon set then there are at least M many a ∈ A+A such that a+1, a−1 ∉ A+A". The Lean states `answer(True) ↔ Tendsto f atTop atTop`, where f n is the minimum of the (truncated-subtraction) isolated-sum count over Sidon subsets of ℕ of size n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Tendsto of the minimum function means: for every M there is N with f n ≥ M for all n ≥ N. That is exactly: every finite Sidon set with |A| ≥ N has at least M isolated sums. The bounded offset between `f` and the source's count is harmless (see the `Erdos152.f` entry). Proved sorry-free: `erdos_152_iff_source : Tendsto f atTop atTop ↔ ∀ M : ℕ, ∃ N, ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Finite → 0 ∉ A → IsSidon A → N ≤ A.ncard → M ≤ cntZ A`. Here `cntZ A` is the number of t ∈ A+A (computed in ℤ) with t±1 ∉ A+A, so the right-hand side is the erdosproblems.com statement word for word (positive integers). Existence of Sidon sets of every size avoiding 0 was proved via `Finset.IsSidon.exists_insert_ge`.

reformulations.difference: The source remarks "There may even be ≫|A|² many such a", now resolved as "This is true, in the stronger sense that there are ≫|A|² many such a". The Lean states `answer(True) ↔ (fun n => f n : ℕ → ℝ) ≫ (fun n => n ^ 2 : ℕ → ℝ)`. The repository's notation (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Basic.lean) unfolds this to `(fun n => (n:ℝ)^2) =O[atTop] (fun n => (f n : ℝ))`, i.e. f(n) ≫ n², read eventually rather than for every n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved sorry-free: `variant_iff_source : (n² =O[atTop] f) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∃ N, ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Finite → 0 ∉ A → IsSidon A → N ≤ A.ncard → c·|A|² ≤ cntZ A`. That is: every sufficiently large finite Sidon set of positive integers has at least c|A|² isolated sums (counted in ℤ). The 'sufficiently large' reading is the only tenable one, because small Sidon sets can have no isolated sums: A = {1,2} gives A+A = {2,3,4}. The direction of `≫` was checked with `#check`.

review.notes:
Both statements are faithful. The cited answers (True, True) and the `research solved` status match erdosproblems.com ("PROVED (LEAN)"; true even in the ≫|A|² sense) and the teorth database ("proved (Lean)").

Lean checks:
- /workspace/review/scratch2.lean: boundary values `f 1 = 0` (via A = {0}), count({0}) = 0 and count({1}) = 1.
- /workspace/review/equiv.lean, sorry-free: `cntN A ≤ cntZ A ≤ cntN A + 1`, `f n ≤ g n ≤ f n + 1`, `tendsto_iff`, `isBigO_iff`, `erdos_152_iff_source` and `variant_iff_source`. These show that both theorem statements are equivalent to the source's wording (positive integers, isolated sums counted in ℤ).

The cited formal proofs [DM26a]/[DM26b] use exactly the same definition of `f` and the same theorem statements, and the line anchors point at the right theorems. I did not re-check them against the current Mathlib: a quick adapted compile hit API drift, which does not bear on the statements.

Minor non-mathematical nuances, not filed as findings:
1. The variant's docstring says the quadratic variant "was also proved formally by the DeepMind prover agent [DM26b]". The erdosproblems.com forum post (GTsoukalas, 3 Apr 2026) says "we formalised the proof of that by hand". In the cited file, the variant is a short hand-written derivation from the agent's lemma f(n) ≥ (n²−100n−16)/16. So the attribution is slightly loose; the mathematics is unaffected.
2. The source's aside "A similar question can be asked for truncations of infinite Sidon sets" is not formalized. The module docstring's TODO acknowledges this.
3. `formal_proof using formal_conjectures` points at a fork, not this repository. This follows the repository's convention: about 60 files cite mo271 fork proofs the same way.

The [ESS94] full text could not be read (ScienceDirect blocks bots). Its open problem was confirmed through O'Bryant's annotated bibliography.
